usage: This is the standard, everyday way to say 'I don't understand' (literally 'I didn't understand') in Moroccan Darija. It is used universally across all regions and levels of formality. Note that Darija uses the past tense form to express immediate lack of understanding of something just said.

variants.label: emphasized
variants.note: Use this to strongly emphasize that you are completely lost.

variants.label: directed at a person
variants.note: Use this to specify that you didn't understand the speaker, rather than the general situation.

variants.label: habitual/general
variants.note: Use this for general inability to understand a language or subject, rather than a specific sentence.

responses.english: I will explain it to you.
Should I repeat it for you?

examples.arabic: سْمَحْ لِيَّا، مَا فْهَمْتْش شْنُو قْلْتِي.
examples.transliteration: sma7 lya, ma fhamtsh shno glti.
examples.english: Sorry, I didn't understand what you said.

examples.arabic: وَاشْ يْمْكْنْ تْعَاوْدْ عَافَاكْ؟ مَا فْهَمْتْش.
examples.english: Can you repeat please? I didn't understand.

examples.arabic: مَا فْهَمْتْش هَادْ لْكْلْمَة، شْنُو كَتْعْنِي؟
examples.transliteration: ma fhamtsh had lklma, shno kat3ni?
examples.english: I don't understand this word, what does it mean?
